message:
cmd/hi: add images subcommand listing pre-pull targets

`hi images tailscale` prints integration.MustTestVersions as
tailscale/tailscale image refs; `hi images golang` prints the Go
toolchain image from go.mod. CI consumes both to pre-pull at job
setup so the per-test runtime never has to hit the Docker Hub
network path, and the version list lives in Go (not duplicated in
shell or YAML).

integration/dockertestutil: add Docker Hub credential resolution

Anonymous Hub pulls hit the 100/6h per-IP ceiling on shared CI
runners, showing up as suite-wide singleton flakes whenever the
runner egress IP crosses the quota.

Credentials() resolves from DOCKERHUB_USERNAME/DOCKERHUB_TOKEN env
vars, then ~/.docker/config.json, then anonymous. AuthConfiguration()
returns dockertest/go-dockerclient auth; RegistryAuth() returns the
base64 form for the modern Docker SDK. PullWithAuth() inspects the
image locally first and only pulls when missing, retrying transient
errors and bailing fast on manifest-unknown.

Neither Docker SDK reads config.json on its own; this helper is the
single source for both surfaces.

cmd/hi: use Docker Hub credentials and retry on image pulls

ensureImageAvailable() passed an empty image.PullOptions, so pulls
ignored docker login state and a transient 429 converted into a
fatal hi doctor FAIL. Pull through dockertestutil.RegistryAuth() and
wrap cli.ImagePull in backoff.Retry; treat manifest-unknown as
permanent so a genuinely missing tag bails fast.

Also add a doctor WARN when no credentials are resolved, so future
contributors who set up the suite locally see the suggestion before
hitting the rate limit.

integration/tsic: pull legacy and unstable images with auth

pool.RunWithOptions() pulls implicitly when an image is missing,
and the dockertest pool's pull path skips ~/.docker/config.json.
Call dockertestutil.PullWithAuth before RunWithOptions in the
unstable and versioned branches; the helper is a no-op when CI's
prepulled-images artefact has already loaded the tag.

ci: authenticate Docker Hub and pre-pull runtime images

Add docker/login-action to the build, build-postgres, and new
build-prepulled jobs of test-integration.yaml, plus the per-test
template. Each login step is guarded by secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME
so PRs from forks (where the secret is absent) skip the step
instead of failing.

build-prepulled runs `hi images tailscale | golang`, docker-pulls
each entry, saves them all as a single tarball, and uploads the
prepulled-images artefact. integration-test-template.yml downloads
and loads the tarball before the test runs, so the runtime SDK pull
paths in tsic and hi doctor never hit the network.

Add a 35-minute timeout-minutes backstop to the test job so a hung
`hi run` cannot hold the runner past its useful lifetime.

integration/integrationutil: add categorised timeout constants

Five redeclarations of `propagationTime := ScaledTimeout(...)` in
route_test.go, plus dozens of inline 200ms-tick literals across the
suite, drift over time and make timing-related flake fixes touch
every test instead of one constant.

Define one variable per category: HAConvergeTimeout,
HASlowConvergeTimeout, PolicyPropagationTimeout, AuthFlowTimeout,
StatusReadyTimeout (each wrapped in ScaledTimeout so CI doubling
stays automatic), plus FastPoll/SlowPoll/PingPoll for tick
intervals. Callsites switch in a follow-up commit.

integration/dockertestutil: extract retry policy and add disconnect helper

retryDockerOp had an inline 30s MaxElapsedTime budget. libnetwork
bridge reprogramming after a back-to-back disconnect/reconnect cycle
has been observed exceeding it on contended GitHub Actions runners,
surfacing in TestHASubnetRouterFailoverDockerDisconnect as:

    API error (500): updating gateway endpoint:
    failed to set gateway: network is unreachable

Move the bounds to constants in retry.go (DockerOpInitialInterval,
DockerOpMaxInterval, DockerOpMaxElapsedTime — 90s, up from 30s).

Add DisconnectAndReconnect: pool.Client.DisconnectNetwork() returns
when the API call is acknowledged, but bridge reprogramming
continues for several seconds. The helper polls
pool.Client.NetworkInfo between the two halves until the
container's endpoint disappears, then reappears with a v4 address.
Callers can still use the bare primitives but opt out of the
settle waits.

integration: add curl-count and policy-loaded check helpers

acl_test.go and route_test.go inline `client.Curl(url) +
assert.Len(result, 13, ...)` 45 times. tsic.Curl returns ("", nil)
on a 0-byte HTTP 200 body, so the NoError check passes and the Len
check fails — EventuallyWithT cannot retry because no error fired.
assertCurlSuccessReturnsCount owns the pair so the future fix to
Curl benefits every site without re-touching the callsites.

assertPolicyLoadedWithCollect polls headscale.DebugFilter for at
least N rules. policyLoadedBarrier wraps the same loop as a
context.Context-aware closure usable with
WaitForTailscaleSyncPerUser's WithPreBarrier option — gating the
peer-sync wait on server-side filter visibility closes the
policy-reload write barrier that the ACL test cluster jumps.

integration: add set-based traceroute first-hop check

assertTracerouteViaIPWithCollect does an exact match on
tr.Route[0].IP at route_test.go:3044. HA failover tests can settle
on any of several valid primaries during convergence; an exact
match flakes during the window even when the eventual state is
correct.

assertTracerouteFirstHopInWithCollect takes a []netip.Addr and
uses assert.Contains so the failure message also shows which set
was allowed. The exact-match helper stays in place; callsites
switch in a follow-up commit.

integration: add SyncOption pre-barrier to peer-sync wait

WaitForTailscaleSyncPerUser only gates on per-client peer-count
parity. After SetPolicy the peer count is unchanged (same user
set), so the gate trips before the new packet filter has been
dispatched. acl_test.go then reads stale state and assert.Len(13)
fails — EventuallyWithT cannot retry because the curl returns
(empty, nil).

Add SyncOption + WithPreBarrier(func(ctx) error). The barrier runs
once before any per-user wait begins, sharing the outer timeout via
context.Context. Default behaviour unchanged for the three existing
callers; tests in ACL/policy paths will swap in a concrete barrier
(see policyLoadedBarrier in helpers.go) in a follow-up commit.

integration/tsic: surface empty curl body as error

tsic.Curl returned ("", nil) when curl exited 0 with a zero-byte
body — the usual signature of a mid-stream reset (HTTP 200 with
the connection torn down before the body arrived). Callers
wrapping the call in EventuallyWithT saw assert.NoError pass and
assert.Len fail with no error to drive a retry, exhausting the
budget on a single tick.

Return errCurlEmptyResponseBody on empty body. The existing
assertion sites already expect non-empty content;
assertCurlFailWithCollect only checks for an error and is
unaffected.

integration: collapse curl+Len inline blocks to helper

The inline `client.Curl(url) + assert.NoError + assert.Len(result, 13,
"expected hostname response")` shape was repeated 56 times across
acl_test.go (32) and route_test.go (24). Pre-G13 tsic.Curl returned
("", nil) on empty bodies and the inline shape let NoError pass while
Len failed, so EventuallyWithT could not retry; the helper now owns
that pair and benefits from the Curl fix without further per-site
changes.

Five callsites in acl_test.go are left inline because their pattern
differs — assert.Lenf with the result variable in the error format,
or per-iteration variadic msgAndArgs, or assert.NotEmpty instead of
Len(13).

Net -114 LOC. Drops `//nolint:unused` from the helper.

integration/dockertestutil: bake libnetwork settle into disconnect primitives

DisconnectContainerFromNetwork and ReconnectContainerToNetwork
returned as soon as the docker API call was acknowledged.
libnetwork bridge reprogramming continued for several seconds
afterwards; a test that disconnected then later reconnected — even
with assertions between — saw "network is unreachable" because the
ConnectNetwork API hit a half-reprogrammed bridge.

Move waitNetworkContainerAbsent and waitNetworkContainerPresent
into the primitives themselves so every caller benefits, not just
the few that wrap them in DisconnectAndReconnect. The composite
helper is now a thin convenience over the two settle-aware
primitives; its settleTimeout argument is preserved for API
compatibility but unused (the primitives drive their own waits
using DockerOpMaxElapsedTime).

This applies to all tests that go through TailscaleClient.Disconnect
FromNetwork/ReconnectToNetwork — including the route_test.go HA
failover phases that mix disconnect/reconnect with assertions in
between.

integration: switch test timeouts to named constants

Replace 295 ad-hoc EventuallyWithT timeout/poll-interval literals
across 11 *_test.go files with the constants from
integrationutil/timeouts.go:

  ScaledTimeout(60s)   → HAConvergeTimeout
  ScaledTimeout(120s)  → HASlowConvergeTimeout
  ScaledTimeout(90s)   → PolicyPropagationTimeout
  ScaledTimeout(30s)   → StatusReadyTimeout
  200ms                → FastPoll
  500ms                → SlowPoll

Only stock values were swapped; non-standard timeouts (e.g.
ScaledTimeout(5*time.Second), per-test pingMatrix scaling, calls
to helpers other than EventuallyWithT) stay inline so the sweep
doesn't fudge deliberate values.

Five `propagationTime := ...` declarations in route_test.go now
reference HAConvergeTimeout / HASlowConvergeTimeout, removing the
drift opportunity between the same-purpose budgets at different
phase blocks.

integration/general_test: replace pacing time.Sleep with ticker

The TestNodeOnlineStatus outer loop sleeps 1 s between iterations
so the continuous online-check does not hammer the docker daemon.
A time.Ticker pre-allocated outside the loop conveys the same
intent without violating the suite-wide "no time.Sleep" rule.

The other eight `time.Sleep` occurrences in integration/ already
have nolint:forbidigo directives because they wait on
wall-clock-driven timers in the system under test (OIDC register
cache expiry, Tailscale 5-min non-HTTPS reconnect cooldown, SSH
check-mode session expiry, DERP updater interval, deliberate
"demonstrate bug timing" log points in tags_test.go). Converting
those needs deeper test redesign per case and is out of scope here.

integration/route_test: move advertise-routes mutation out of EventuallyWithT

cmd/hi/README.md forbids state-mutating calls inside EventuallyWithT:
retrying a mutation can mask real failures and double-apply side
effects. The advertise-routes setup loop violated this by running
`tailscale set --advertise-routes=...` inside the retry block.

Split into two steps: a retry that reads status (Self.ID may not be
populated immediately after connection), then a one-shot Execute
guarded by require.NoErrorf — failures now bubble up directly
instead of being absorbed by the retry budget.

ci: rotate TestHASubnetRouterFailover into postgres matrix

The postgres matrix has run with five stable tests since it was
introduced; its 0 % flake rate is sampling bias, not a signal
about postgres reliability. Add TestHASubnetRouterFailover (12.8 %
flake rate on sqlite) so the two backends can be compared
side-by-side on the same test.

A clean postgres signal points at a sqlite-only timing window;
equal flakiness points at the NodeStore / mapper logic above the
storage layer. Either outcome guides the next round of hardening.

ci: drop pre-pull job

Docker Hub auth on the build and test jobs is enough on its own;
the build-prepulled job, hi images subcommand, and the postgres
matrix rotation can go.

Closes #3261 review comments on pre-pull and postgres rotation.
integration/dockertestutil: drop unused settleTimeout arg from DisconnectAndReconnect
ci: drop timeout-minutes backstop on integration test job

integration: rename curl helper to assertCurlDockerHostname

The 13-byte length is the Docker auto-generated container hostname
(12 hex chars + newline from /etc/hostname). Naming the helper after
what it actually checks beats parametrising a literal that never
varies; the unparam lint that fired on the previous signature goes
away.

integration: tighten doc comments

Drop paragraphs that restated what the diff already shows. Keep the
non-obvious WHY in one line per identifier.

ci: drop Docker v28 pin in favour of overlay2 storage driver

Docker 29 itself works; the runner-image change that broke the
suite was the overlayfs default. Setting storage-driver=overlay2
restores the previous behaviour and lets us run on the current
Docker without the apt downgrade dance.

If anything regresses, revert to the pin.

integration/acl_test: gate autogroup:self wait on filter change

snapshotPolicyFilter captures DebugFilter rule count before SetPolicy;
policyChangedBarrier blocks WaitForTailscaleSyncPerUser until the
count differs. Without this gate, the peer-count wait trips before
the new policy is compiled server-side and the curl assertion fires
on stale state.

Renames policyLoadedBarrier(minRules) to policyChangedBarrier(baseline)
— the absolute-count form was never reachable because callers don't
know the post-SetPolicy count in advance.

integration: wait on client-side filter and widen HA failover budget

`policyChangedBarrier` only checked server-side filter rule count.
The Phase 2 connectivity assertion still raced ahead of the
client-side wgengine applying the new PacketFilter. Replace with
`snapshotClientFilters` + `waitForClientFilterChange`: snapshot each
client's netmap.PacketFilter before SetPolicy, then poll until each
client's filter fingerprint differs.

TestHASubnetRouterFailover propagationTime is now HASlowConverge
Timeout. Even after PrimaryRoutes flips server-side and is reflected
in client.Status, tailscale's wgengine sometimes keeps routing
through the previous primary for ~2 min. Doubling the budget gives
the data plane room to catch up; the exact-match traceroute hop
assertion stays.

Drop the unused assertTracerouteFirstHopInWithCollect helper — its
set-based semantics would have weakened the data-plane check rather
than waiting for it.

integration: widen post-policy propagation budget on slow CI

PolicyPropagationTimeout was 90 s; the Phase 2 connectivity assertion
in TestACLPolicyPropagationOverTime kept exhausting it on contended
CI runners even though wgengine eventually applied the new packet
filter. Bump to 180 s (360 s on CI) — matches what local repro and
the HA tests already use for data-plane convergence.

Point TestACLGroupAfterUserDeletion's post-CreateUser assertions at
PolicyPropagationTimeout rather than HAConvergeTimeout; the wait is
about policy reload propagating to clients, not HA primary
re-election.

integration/acl_test: use PolicyPropagationTimeout for ExactReproduction post-CreateUser waits

Same fix already applied to TestACLGroupAfterUserDeletion (which now
passes). The ExactReproduction sites still used HAConvergeTimeout
(120s on CI) and timed out before the post-policy reload completed
on slow runners.

mapper: include UserProfiles in policy-change MapResponses

policyChangeResponse populated PeersChanged for cross-user peers but
left UserProfiles unset. The Tailscale netmap accumulates UserProfiles
incrementally and looks up each peer's user via the per-session cache.
When the cache is missing an entry, the peer surfaces in the netmap
without a UserProfiles[user] binding. On slow CI the resulting peer
set is fragile and same-user reachability tests stall until the cache
happens to be repopulated by a later non-policy event.

Fixes TestACLPolicyPropagationOverTime flakes at the Phase 2
EventuallyWithT block that exercises autogroup:self for the first time.

state: defer HA failover when probe target reconnected mid-cycle

The HA prober dispatches a PingRequest, waits ProbeTimeout (5s by
default), and marks the node Unhealthy if no callback arrives. A
node that bounced its poll session between probe cycles satisfies
two conditions that conspire to fail TestHASubnetRouterFailover on
slow CI runners:

  - A probe queued against the previous session is silently dropped
    when the worker tries to write to the closed connection, so the
    timeout always fires.
  - A probe sent immediately after reconnect lands while wgengine
    is still rebuilding magicsock state from the new netmap; the
    client cannot answer within 5s.

Either path installs a spurious Unhealthy bit, which kicks the
preserved-primary anti-flap into the wrong choice: the test removes
the route approval from the standing primary expecting failover to
router 1, but router 2 wins because router 1 was wrongly tagged
Unhealthy during the bring-up window.

Track the SessionEpoch observed at probe-dispatch time and bail out
in the timeout path if the node has reconnected since. Track the
last epoch the prober observed for each node and require an epoch
to survive a full probe cycle before letting a timeout drive a
failover. The recovery side and the existing "no approved routes"
guard in SetNodeUnhealthy are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

integration/dockertestutil: wait for stale subnet routes to clear before reconnect

DisconnectContainerFromNetwork returned as soon as libnetwork's own
endpoint view dropped the container. The container's kernel netns
keeps the subnet route entry for a brief window after that. A
subsequent ConnectNetwork on the same network then tries to assign
the sticky IP and libnetwork refuses with "cannot program address
... conflicts with existing route", surfacing as a 500 to the docker
client and propagating up through ReconnectToNetwork.

Reproducer: TestHASubnetRouterFailoverDockerDisconnect phase 4c,
which cable-pulls r2 (172.24.0.5/16) and immediately reconnects.

Extend the disconnect settle wait to poll "ip route show" in the
container until no route for the network's IPAM subnet remains. As
a belt-and-braces step, on ConnectNetwork failure whose error matches
the route-conflict 500, drop the surviving route via "ip route del"
inside the container and let the existing retry budget reissue the
ConnectNetwork call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

mapper: include DNSConfig in policy-change MapResponses

policyChangeResponse omitted DNSConfig, so policy churn produced
MapResponses where the client's netmap DNS was implicitly carried over
from the previous snapshot. On slow CI runners, the wgengine reconfigure
that follows an autogroup:self transition flips tsdev's IP set
(fe80-only -> tunnel IPs) and triggers a major LinkChange while DNS is
being re-applied. The LinkChange handler reapplies dns.Manager.Set with
the engine's lastDNSConfig snapshot; if that snapshot is stale, the OS
resolver loses both the 65 MagicDNS reverse-DNS routes and the
100.100.100.100 forwarder, and curl-by-FQDN returns empty body for the
remainder of the policy window.

Re-asserting DNSConfig on every policy change keeps lastDNSConfig fresh
through that race so the post-LinkChange OScfg retains Nameservers and
Routes. The CI artefacts at iteration 1 Phase 2 show the OS resolver
going from {Nameservers:[100.100.100.100 ...]} to {SearchDomains only}
across a single LinkChange tick; with the policy MapResponse carrying
DNSConfig, the second Set uses the full netmap DNS instead.

Fixes TestACLPolicyPropagationOverTime, TestACLGroupAfterUserDeletion,
and TestACLGroupDeletionExactReproduction flakes that surface on slow CI
even with the UserProfiles fix in place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
